correctness.rationale: Vertex constraints suffice by expressing a boundary point as a convex combination containing a vertex of its minimal supporting face. Summing the vertex illumination inequalities gives total mass >=f0/alpha; averaging a maximizing direction under a vertex-transitive symmetry group achieves exactly f0/alpha. Polar active inequalities convert vertex illumination into dual facets strictly inside one central halfspace. From the actual 20 triangular icosahedral facets and 12 pentagonal dodecahedral facets, independent exhaustive antipodal-transversal enumeration found distributions {0:12,1:20,4:20,5:12} over 64 and {0:740,1:204,2:60,3:20} over 1024, yielding alpha(D)=5 and alpha(I)=3 once explicit genuine halfspaces in verify.py attain these maxima. Independently recomputed all 495 4-tuples among the twelve size-five facet sets: none covers twenty, so i(D)>4; the five explicit dual halfspace normals in RESULT.md/verify.py give i(D)<=5. Thus i*(D)=i*(I)=4 and i(D)=5, gap5/4. Finite counts are exhaustive only for these fixed Platonic duals, not a dimension-uniform theorem.
